executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO covering late 2025 through May 2026 identify multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated repeated epidemiological updates in the Americas region, indicating sustained zoonotic transmission risk with pandemic potential. Mpox (BSL-3 select agent) continues circulating in the Americas, while dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever present significant arboviral burden across Latin America. Pertussis resurgence, measles importation risk, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season add further complexity to the regional threat landscape.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) and Mpox represent the highest-priority select agent threats, compounded by simultaneous arboviral surges and vaccine-preventable disease resurgence across the Americas.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained regional activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoir with pandemic potential
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in human infections
Animal-to-human transmission events requiring enhanced surveillance and response
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance protocols; strengthen human-animal interface monitoring; ensure health worker PPE and antiviral stockpiles; coordinate with agriculture sector on poultry outbreak containment

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating ongoing regional transmission
BSL-3 select agent requiring high-containment laboratory procedures
Continued circulation across multiple countries in the Americas
Risk of further spread given ongoing community transmission
threats.action: Reinforce contact tracing and ring vaccination strategies; ensure diagnostic capacity with BSL-3 protocols; monitor for clade-specific variants; coordinate cross-border surveillance with national health authorities

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 18 2026 signaling high case burden
Historically elevated transmission season with risk of severe dengue
Multiple serotypes co-circulating increasing risk of severe disease in previously exposed populations
Vector control challenges amid climate-related Aedes mosquito range expansion
threats.action: Intensify vector control programs; enhance clinical surveillance for severe dengue; ensure blood product safety; issue public health advisories on personal protection measures

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating active cases
BSL-3 pathogen with high mortality in unvaccinated individuals
Risk of urban transmission if Aedes aegypti vectors are present
Potential for international spread via unvaccinated travelers
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers; investigate epizootic activity in non-human primates; enforce vaccination certificate requirements at borders; coordinate with WHO on International Health Regulations notifications

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Viruses
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert issued April 27 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Earlier PAHO alert from January 2026 flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation
Transition from Northern to Southern Hemisphere season creating continuous global transmission pressure
Potential strain mismatch risk between circulating strains and vaccine formulations
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere vaccination campaigns; enhance syndromic surveillance for influenza-like illness; strengthen hospital surge capacity; monitor for novel reassortant strains

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating resurgence
Increasing case counts suggesting waning vaccine immunity or coverage gaps
Risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised individuals
Potential for healthcare-associated transmission
threats.action: Review and reinforce vaccination coverage especially in pregnant women and infants; strengthen laboratory diagnostic capacity; issue clinical guidance on case management; investigate outbreak clusters for transmission chains

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue complicating clinical diagnosis
Aedes mosquito vector expansion driven by climate and urbanization factors
Risk of severe outcomes in elderly and immunocompromised populations
threats.action: Strengthen integrated arboviral surveillance distinguishing chikungunya from dengue; intensify vector control; provide clinical guidance on differentiation and management; monitor for importation to non-endemic areas

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026 indicating importation and transmission risk
Vaccination coverage gaps creating susceptible population pockets
Risk of outbreak in under-vaccinated communities given high transmissibility (R0 12-18)
Potential for re-establishment of endemic transmission in regions that had achieved elimination
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination coverage assessments; implement supplemental immunization activities in low-coverage areas; strengthen case-based surveillance and outbreak response capacity; enforce international travel vaccination recommendations

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are actively flagged in current surveillance: (1) Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — subject to two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025, March 2026) indicating sustained zoonotic activity in the Americas with pandemic risk; high-containment laboratory protocols and enhanced One Health surveillance are required. (2) Mpox (Monkeypox virus) — subject to a PAHO epidemiological update in April 2026 confirming ongoing regional transmission; BSL-3 handling protocols and targeted vaccination are critical countermeasures. Yellow fever virus, while not a US Select Agent, is a WHO-priority pathogen warranting equivalent vigilance given its high mortality and outbreak potential flagged in March 2026.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals detected in available report titles and descriptions; Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance warrants monitoring given resurgence signals
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) should be monitored in H5N1 strains given sustained animal reservoir activity
Healthcare-associated transmission risk during pertussis resurgence may select for antibiotic-resistant strains in clinical settings
emergingPatterns: Concurrent arboviral threats (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) suggest sustained Aedes mosquito vector pressure across the Americas, potentially amplified by climate-driven range expansion
Repeated PAHO alerts on H5N1 across two reporting periods (Nov 2025, Mar 2026) indicate persistent zoonotic spillover risk rather than isolated events
Simultaneous resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) points to systemic vaccination coverage gaps across the Americas region
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset in April 2026 combined with ongoing RSV co-circulation creates elevated respiratory disease burden period
The volume of ECDC communicable disease threat reports across five consecutive weeks (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) suggests sustained elevated threat activity in Europe requiring further detail
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) and GLP-1 medication misuse alert (February 2026) indicate non-infectious public health threats compounding infectious disease burden on health systems
